args.summary: Short run on Qwen3.5-9B (L28-31 MLP, unembedding-subspace scoring with a 1.5x penalty on other categories). Findings: (1) Month-subspace clusters (256 units) at L31 and L30 IMPROVED month_successor when ablated (-.278 / -.077) with controls flat, so they act as month suppressors or competitors, not month writers. The L28 version was inert. (2) The L31 plural-subspace 256 cluster was inert on plural_nouns (.024). (3) The L31 Roman-numeral-subspace 256 cluster did nothing for roman_numeral (.014) but cut ordinal_words .302 (control .064, weekday .067). Its screen failed because one random 256-unit L31 part dropped ordinal .35. L31 ordinal is diffuse enough that random parts sometimes hit it. 1 screen used, 0 passed.

agent:
This short run on Qwen3.5-9B found no new part: I screened one candidate and it failed.

I picked 256-neuron groups in the MLPs of layers 28–31, scoring each neuron by how strongly it writes toward a category's output words while penalising the other categories.

- **Month (layers 30–31):** removing these groups made month_successor better, not worse (by .278 at layer 31 and .077 at layer 30), with controls flat. They seem to push down month answers rather than write them. The layer 28 group did nothing.
- **Plural nouns (layer 31):** no real effect on plural_nouns (.024).
- **Roman numerals (layer 31):** no effect on roman_numeral (.014), but it cut ordinal_words by .302. Its control moved .064 and weekday .067. The screen failed because one of the five random 256-neuron groups from layer 31 cut ordinal_words by .35. Ordinal handling there is spread out enough that random groups can hit it.
